purpose: Give callisto consumers a working, documented mechanism that places CI-built native binary artifacts (napi-rs .node files, maturin wheels) into their platform-stub package directories before `callisto publish` runs, closing the gap between `callisto matrix`'s output and a working end-to-end release, with artifact names that stay unique when multiple packages in one workspace share a target triple.
scope: Two changes. (1) Rust: `crates/callisto-graph/src/matrix.rs`'s `artifact_name_for_triple(triple: &str) -> String` is replaced with `artifact_name_for_package_triple(package_name: &str, triple: &str) -> String`, returning `format!("native-{package_name}-{triple}")`; `build_platform_target` (already receiving `package_name` as a parameter) is updated to call it. This embeds the already-workspace-unique `package_name` (a value `PlatformTarget` already carries, sourced from each package's own identity) into `artifactName`, so two different packages declaring the same triple no longer produce colliding CI artifact names. (2) GitHub Actions: extends `.github/actions/callisto-action/action.yml`'s existing `callisto-orchestrate` composite-action step -- within the block already guarded by `[[ -n "$INPUT_PUBLISH" && "$INPUT_PUBLISH" != "false" ]]` (action.yml:167), immediately after `NATIVE_MATRIX` is computed, adds a placement loop that downloads each `nativeMatrix` entry's artifact by `artifactName` (pinned to the current run via `$GITHUB_RUN_ID`) and places its contents into `packageDir`. Also updates `.claude/specs/callisto-matrix.md` §6.2 and corrects `ARCHITECTURE.md` §12's broken example workflow.
non_goals: Extending PlatformTargetKind to Java/JNI or .NET native-AOT targets -- a separate, later concern; this spec only routes the two kinds PlatformTargetKind already supports (Napi, Maturin).
Prebuilt Rust CLI binaries distributed as GitHub Release assets ("Tier 2") -- a separate, related, deferred future spec.
Homebrew tap formula generation/distribution -- deferred by the maintainer as a possible separate future tool.
Go binary distribution -- already an existing non-goal per .claude/specs/callisto-matrix.md §8, not being revisited here.

A generic callisto-build-action that dispatches the actual per-platform build (napi build --platform --release, etc.) -- callisto-matrix.md §7's secondary/optional proposal. This spec covers only placement of an already-built, correctly-named artifact; the build step itself is the consumer's own responsibility.

Validating the content of a downloaded artifact (e.g. confirming a .node file is well-formed, or that it is actually a valid binary for its target triple). The placement step moves whatever files gh run download retrieves into packageDir; content correctness is the build job's responsibility and surfaces later, at publish or install time, not at placement.

Adding a new required input to callisto-action to opt into placement. Placement is driven entirely by whether nativeMatrix is a non-empty array -- consumers with no native platform targets see zero behavior change.

Implementing the nonexistent callisto publish-target Rust CLI subcommand referenced by ARCHITECTURE.md §12's status note (line 447). That subcommand is not needed for this requirement and is not built by this spec; the status note's reference to it (alongside Java/.NET native-AOT discovery) remains accurate and is deliberately left in place -- only the example workflow's own code block, which currently invokes the nonexistent subcommand directly and dereferences nonexistent matrix.os/matrix.package/matrix.target fields, is corrected.

Guaranteeing that a binary placed at packageDir by this step is picked up and included in callisto publish's registry upload output (npm tarball, PyPI wheel, etc.). That round-trip guarantee is owned by whatever spec governs callisto publish's own native-binary packaging logic (crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/publish.rs) -- this spec's guarantee ends at the file being present on disk at packageDir before publish begins.

Handling malformed or invalid-JSON nativeMatrix values within callisto-action's own in-step placement loop. NATIVE_MATRIX (action.yml:164) is produced and consumed entirely within one shell step under `set -o pipefail`, with `jq` already validating JSON syntax (and failing the step via `|| { echo "::error::callisto matrix failed"; exit 1; }`) before the placement loop added by this spec ever reads the value -- malformed JSON cannot reach this specific loop by construction. This does not apply to a consumer's own custom multi-job pipeline built against callisto-matrix.md §6.2's standalone reference snippet, where nativeMatrix genuinely crosses a job-output boundary; that snippet's own error handling is out of scope for this spec beyond the run-id pin AC-011 requires.

Handling a missing (absent-key) or null artifactName/packageDir field on an otherwise-valid nativeMatrix entry. crates/callisto-model/src/matrix.rs's PlatformTarget declares both fields as plain `String` (not `Option<String>`), so serde can never serialize a missing or null value for either field into the JSON callisto matrix emits.

Preserving the exact literal string format `native-{triple}` (no package-name component) as a stable, versioned contract of callisto matrix's JSON output. This spec deliberately changes artifactName's value (adding a package_name segment) to fix the collision defect; a consumer that hardcoded the old two-segment format rather than treating artifactName as an opaque per-entry correlation token (its documented purpose) will observe a different string. No config override for this naming scheme is provided -- package_name is already sourced from the package's own identity, which is already user-configurable through the normal manifest name field; a separate artifact-naming override would duplicate that control for no benefit, since the artifact name is a CI-internal correlation id, never published or user-facing.

api_surface.name: artifact_name_for_package_triple
api_surface.description: Replaces `artifact_name_for_triple(triple: &str) -> String`. Returns `format!("native-{package_name}-{triple}")`. `build_platform_target` (crates/callisto-graph/src/matrix.rs:126-142), which already receives `package_name` as its third parameter, calls this instead of the old triple-only function when constructing `PlatformTarget.artifact_name`.

api_surface.name: callisto-action native artifact placement loop
api_surface.signature: New shell logic inside `.github/actions/callisto-action/action.yml`'s existing `callisto-orchestrate` composite step, placed inside the `[[ -n "$INPUT_PUBLISH" && "$INPUT_PUBLISH" != "false" ]]` guard (action.yml:167) immediately after `NATIVE_MATRIX` is computed (action.yml:164-165) and before `callisto plan-publish`/publish executes.
api_surface.description: Feeds `NATIVE_MATRIX` through process substitution, not a pipe -- `while IFS= read -r ENTRY; do ... done < <(printf '%s' "$NATIVE_MATRIX" | jq -c '.[]')` -- matching the existing pattern used for the releases loop at action.yml:219, so an `exit 1` inside the loop body terminates the step itself, not a subshell. For each ENTRY: extracts `ARTIFACT=$(echo "$ENTRY" | jq -r '.artifactName')` and `DIR_RAW=$(echo "$ENTRY" | jq -r '.packageDir')`; sets `DIR` to `.` when `DIR_RAW` is the empty string (the real value `packageDir` takes for a workspace-root package, per crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/matrix.rs:34-39), otherwise `DIR=$DIR_RAW`; runs `mkdir -p "$DIR"` explicitly; then runs `gh run download "$GITHUB_RUN_ID" --name "$ARTIFACT" --dir "$DIR" || { echo "::error::failed to download artifact '$ARTIFACT' for placement into '$DIR' within run $GITHUB_RUN_ID"; exit 1; }`. Runs once per array element, in array order. Skipped entirely (loop body never executes) when `NATIVE_MATRIX` is `[]`.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given two distinct packages in the same workspace that each declare the same platform target triple (e.g. both declare x86_64-apple-darwin), `callisto matrix --format json`'s output contains two distinct entries for that triple -- one per package -- and their `artifactName` values differ, each equal to `native-<that package's packageName>-<triple>`.

Given the same two-packages-one-triple scenario as AC-001, `.github/actions/callisto-action/action.yml`'s `NATIVE_MATRIX` computation (which pipes callisto matrix's output through `unique_by(.artifactName)`) retains both packages' entries rather than collapsing them to one, because their artifactName values are now distinct.

Given a workflow run where N per-platform build jobs each upload an artifact via actions/upload-artifact using the exact artifactName string from that platform's callisto matrix --format json entry, and the callisto-orchestrate step's placement loop (placed inside the `[[ -n "$INPUT_PUBLISH" && "$INPUT_PUBLISH" != "false" ]]` guard, not merely somewhere after NATIVE_MATRIX computation) executes: after the step completes, each of the N artifacts' downloaded file contents are present under the corresponding packageDir path relative to the working directory (with the directory having been created via the loop's own mkdir -p if it did not already exist), and this placement completes before the step's callisto plan-publish/publish invocation begins.

Given nativeMatrix is [] (no native platform-target packages in the workspace) and INPUT_PUBLISH is non-empty and not the literal string "false" (so the guard at action.yml:167 is entered), the placement loop body never executes (zero gh run download invocations) because NATIVE_MATRIX's parsed array is empty, and the step proceeds directly to callisto plan-publish/publish exactly as it did before this change. Given INPUT_PUBLISH is unset or the literal string "false", the placement loop is never reached regardless of nativeMatrix's contents, because the loop is placed inside that same guard.

Given a nativeMatrix entry whose packageDir field is the empty string (the value produced for a workspace-root package whose manifest has no parent directory component), the placement loop sets DIR to "." before calling mkdir -p and gh run download --dir, and the corresponding artifact's contents are placed directly under the working directory rather than the step failing or attempting mkdir -p with an empty path.

Given a nativeMatrix entry whose artifactName was never uploaded within the current workflow run ($GITHUB_RUN_ID) -- including the case where an artifact with that exact name exists in a different, older, or unrelated workflow run in the same repository -- the loop's `gh run download "$GITHUB_RUN_ID" --name "$ARTIFACT" --dir "$DIR"` invocation exits non-zero because the run-id pins the lookup to the current run only, the `|| { ...; exit 1; }` clause terminates the step (not merely a pipeline subshell) before reaching callisto plan-publish/publish, and the step's log output names the specific missing artifactName and the DIR value (post `.`-normalization where applicable) that download attempt was targeting.

ARCHITECTURE.md §12's example workflow code block (the fenced code block following the "Zero-Config GitHub Actions Workflow Pattern" heading) contains no occurrence of the string "callisto publish-target" anywhere within it; the status note above the heading (naming Java/JNI, .NET native-AOT, and the callisto publish-target subcommand as unimplemented) is unchanged and still present.

ARCHITECTURE.md §12's example workflow's build job step references only field names that exist on PlatformTarget's actual camelCase JSON serialization (triple, platform, arch, abi, hostRunner, useCross, artifactName, packageDir, packageName) -- specifically, it does not reference matrix.os, matrix.package, or matrix.target (none of which are real fields), and its `runs-on:` uses `${{ matrix.hostRunner }}`.

ARCHITECTURE.md §12's example workflow, read end to end, shows all of: a build job producing and uploading a per-platform artifact, a placement step downloading that artifact into its package directory, and a callisto publish (or callisto-action with publish enabled) step running afterward against the populated package directories -- not just the build step.

A consumer workflow that already uses callisto-action for publishing and adds only a matrix-driven build job (per .claude/specs/callisto-matrix.md §6.1's nativeMatrix consumption pattern) uploading artifacts named per artifactName, with no additional bash, composite action, or script authored by the consumer to perform placement, ends with the callisto-orchestrate step having invoked gh run download once per nativeMatrix entry and each entry's artifact contents present at that entry's packageDir (post `.`-normalization) -- with no requirement on this spec's part that callisto publish itself subsequently succeeds, per this spec's non-goal on the publish-side packaging round-trip.

.claude/specs/callisto-matrix.md §6.2's standalone reference snippet (for consumers building their own custom multi-job pipeline outside callisto-action, where nativeMatrix genuinely crosses a `needs.<job>.outputs.nativeMatrix` job-output boundary) is updated to pin the download to `$GITHUB_RUN_ID` and to `mkdir -p "$DIR"` before calling `gh run download`, and §6.2 gains an explicit note stating that consumers using callisto-action for publishing do not need to write this snippet themselves -- callisto-action performs equivalent placement automatically, in-step, once nativeMatrix is non-empty and publish is enabled.

reasoning: Third revision, responding to canon:exit-gate's second fail verdict (retry_count 2, 5 blockers, high confidence). The load-bearing new finding: artifact_name_for_triple(triple) ignores package_name entirely, so two different packages declaring the same triple produce identical artifactName values, and the existing unique_by(.artifactName) dedup in action.yml (added to avoid redundant downloads, per its own comment) silently collapses them to one entry -- defeating placement for the second package. Root cause traced to crates/callisto-graph/src/matrix.rs:38-40 (artifact_name_for_triple) and confirmed PlatformTarget already carries package_name (crates/callisto-model/src/matrix.rs:70, threaded through from the package's own identity, workspace-unique by construction per PackageId uniqueness) but never uses it in artifact_name. Fix scope now includes a real Rust change: artifact_name_for_triple is replaced with artifact_name_for_package_triple(package_name, triple), embedding the already-unique package_name -- mirroring napi-rs's own convention of naming published platform-stub packages <package-name>-<platform>-<arch> for exactly the same disambiguation reason. Deliberately not made config-overridable: package_name already flows from the package's own, already-configurable identity, and the artifact name itself is a CI-internal correlation id (never published, never user-facing) with no independent reason to need its own override surface -- adding one would duplicate existing configurability for no benefit, matching this project's stated preference for leaning on existing mechanisms over inventing bespoke config. AC-001/AC-002 are new, testing the fix directly at both the Rust JSON-output level and the Action's dedup-consuming level. The remaining four blockers were addressed precisely: guard placement is now explicit in AC-003/AC-004's text (loop lives inside the INPUT_PUBLISH guard, not merely after NATIVE_MATRIX computation, closing the gap where an implementation could place the loop ungated); AC-006(old AC-004)'s log-message wording now says 'the DIR value (post normalization)' rather than implying it must equal the raw JSON packageDir field, resolving the AC-005/AC-006 contradiction the gate found for the root-package case; ARCHITECTURE.md's example fix is now split into AC-007 (string removal) and AC-008 (real field names -- hostRunner/packageName/triple, not the fictional matrix.os/matrix.package/matrix.target the gate found still dereferenced), both required together; and callisto-matrix.md §6.2 (AC-011, old AC-008) is no longer claimed to 'match this spec's mechanism' -- instead it's corrected as its own standalone reference for the genuinely-different cross-job pattern a consumer might build without callisto-action, with a cross-reference note pointing at callisto-action's automatic handling, resolving the gate's finding that AC-008(old) left the cross-job MATRIX_JSON snippet's structural mismatch with the 'no cross-job boundary' non-goal reasoning unaddressed.
